title: Restaurant, cafe, bar, hotel or venue
basis: Recalled general knowledge, 2026-10-22; hosts not re-fetched (UNVERIFIED). Reservation and delivery platforms rarely pass followed links; their value is bookings, reviews and being named in answers.

domainTypes.note: claim the listing; reviews and photos
only if the restaurant takes reservations there
city 'best of' maps; pitch the chef or a new opening

patterns.why: a tourism board or convention and visitors bureau (member listings)
a food blog, restaurant week or food festival site
a supplier whose 'where to eat' page can name the restaurant

angles: Claim Google, Tripadvisor and Apple Maps listings; keep the menu, hours and photos current there first.
Join the chamber and the tourism board; their visitor guides and member pages link to restaurants.
Ask the farms, brewers and roasters you buy from to name the restaurant on their 'where to find us' page.
Pitch the local food writer a story (a new dish, a chef's background, a charity night) a few weeks ahead.
Take part in restaurant week and local food festivals; the event pages list participants with a link.
Answer reviews on Google and Tripadvisor politely and quickly.
avoid: Paying food bloggers for a review without them marking it as sponsored (FTC disclosure rules apply in the US, and Google expects rel="sponsored").
Offering free meals or discounts in exchange for positive reviews.
Listing the business under extra fake locations or ghost kitchens' names to appear in more places.
Buying followers or 'voting' packages for readers' polls.
